en.greeting: Hi! Today we talk about two important things: your family and your home. We'll learn the words in small groups, then you'll describe a home in a few short sentences.

steps.title: Your close family
steps.text: Let's start with the people closest to you.
steps.body: Your **parents** are your mother and father (orang tua — always with -s). Brothers and sisters together are **siblings**. English shows if they are a man or a woman: **brother** or **sister**. Kakak = **older** brother/sister, adik = **younger** brother/sister. Your children are your **sons** and **daughters**.

steps.title: The wider family
steps.text: Now the bigger family you see at Lebaran.
steps.body: Your parents' parents are your **grandparents**: **grandmother** (nenek) and **grandfather** (kakek). Your parents' brothers are your **uncles**, their sisters are your **aunts**. Their children are your **cousins** — one word for boys and girls, like sepupu.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Think about who is who in Sari's family.

question.prompt: Sari's mother has a sister, Wulan. Who is Wulan to Sari?
question.explanation: Your mother's sister is your **aunt** (tante / bibi). Wulan's children are Sari's **cousins**, and Sari's **grandmother** is her mother's mother.

steps.title: Talking about family
steps.text: Here's how people talk about their family. Read them out loud.
steps.body: Count brothers and sisters together as **siblings**: *three siblings: two brothers and one sister*, never 'three brothers: two boys and one girl'.

examples.en: My parents live in Medan.
examples.id: Orang tua saya tinggal di Medan.

examples.en: I have three siblings: two brothers and one sister.
examples.id: Saya punya tiga saudara kandung: dua laki-laki dan satu perempuan.

examples.en: My younger brother is a student.
examples.id: Adik laki-laki saya seorang pelajar.

examples.en: Pak Joko and his wife have two daughters.
examples.id: Pak Joko dan istrinya punya dua anak perempuan.

examples.en: My cousin Reza works in Bali.
examples.id: Sepupu saya, Reza, bekerja di Bali.

steps.title: Listen
steps.text: Rina talks about her home. Press play and listen.

question.prompt: Listen to Rina. Who does she live with?
question.listen: I live in Surabaya with my parents and my grandmother.
question.explanation: Rina says **my parents and my grandmother**: her mother, her father and her nenek.

steps.title: Rooms and furniture
steps.text: Now let's walk through a house.
steps.body: Rooms: **living room** (ruang tamu / ruang keluarga), **bedroom**, **kitchen**, **bathroom**. Kamar alone can be any room, so be clear: kamar tidur = **bedroom**, kamar mandi = **bathroom**. Just say **the kitchen**, not 'the kitchen room'. Furniture: **bed**, **sofa**, **wardrobe** (for clothes), **table**, **chair**, **fridge**.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Which room is it?

question.prompt: In the evening, Budi's family sits on the sofa and watches TV. Which room are they in?
question.explanation: The sofa and the TV are usually in the **living room** (ruang keluarga). There is no 'kitchen room' in English — it's just **the kitchen**.

steps.title: Describing a home
steps.text: To describe a home, say where, who and what. Look at these.
steps.body: **Where:** I live in a house / a flat in ... **Who:** I live with ... **What:** My house **has** ... (my house = it, so **has**). Put the adjective before the noun: a **big** bedroom.

examples.en: I live in a small flat in Jakarta.
examples.id: Saya tinggal di apartemen kecil di Jakarta.

examples.en: I live with my wife and my son.
examples.id: Saya tinggal dengan istri dan anak laki-laki saya.

examples.en: Our house has four bedrooms and a garden.
examples.id: Rumah kami punya empat kamar tidur dan sebuah kebun.

examples.en: My bedroom has a bed, a desk and a wardrobe.
examples.id: Di kamar tidur saya ada tempat tidur, meja dan lemari pakaian.

examples.en: The living room is big and bright.
examples.id: Ruang keluarganya besar dan terang.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Pak Joko tells you about his flat. Which sentence is correct?

question.explanation: My flat = it, so use **has** (punya): **My flat has two bedrooms.** 'Have' is for I, you, we, they, and 'is two bedrooms' says the flat IS two bedrooms.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now describe a kitchen.

question.prompt: Arrange the words: Dapur kami kecil tapi bersih.
question.solution: Our kitchen is small but clean.
question.explanation: Start with the room (**Our kitchen**), then **is** + adjective. **But** joins two different ideas: small, but clean.

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here are all the words on one page. Keep it for later.

Say **the kitchen**, not `the kitchen room`. Kamar tidur = **bedroom**, kamar mandi = **bathroom**.
My house / my flat = it, so: **My house has** two bedrooms.

examples.id: Saya tinggal di rumah di Bandung.

examples.en: I live with my parents and my sister.
examples.id: Saya tinggal dengan orang tua dan saudara perempuan saya.

steps.text: Want more? Read a short email about a family and practise words for your home.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kita membahas dua hal penting: keluargamu dan rumahmu. Kita belajar kata-katanya dalam kelompok kecil, lalu kamu mendeskripsikan rumah dalam beberapa kalimat pendek.

steps.title: Keluarga inti
steps.text: Kita mulai dari orang-orang terdekatmu.
steps.body: **Parents** adalah ibu dan ayahmu (orang tua — selalu pakai -s). Saudara laki-laki dan perempuan bersama-sama disebut **siblings**. Bahasa Inggris menunjukkan laki-laki atau perempuan: **brother** atau **sister**. Kakak = **older** brother/sister, adik = **younger** brother/sister. Anak-anakmu adalah **sons** (laki-laki) dan **daughters** (perempuan).

steps.title: Keluarga besar
steps.text: Sekarang keluarga besar yang kamu temui saat Lebaran.
steps.body: Orang tua dari orang tuamu adalah **grandparents**: **grandmother** (nenek) dan **grandfather** (kakek). Saudara laki-laki orang tuamu adalah **uncles**, saudara perempuannya **aunts**. Anak-anak mereka adalah **cousins** — satu kata untuk laki-laki dan perempuan, sama seperti sepupu.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pikirkan siapa saja di keluarga Sari.

question.prompt: Ibu Sari punya saudara perempuan, Wulan. Siapa Wulan bagi Sari?
question.explanation: Saudara perempuan ibumu adalah **aunt** (tante / bibi). Anak-anak Wulan adalah **cousins** (sepupu) Sari, dan **grandmother** Sari adalah ibu dari ibunya.

steps.title: Bercerita tentang keluarga
steps.text: Begini cara orang bercerita tentang keluarganya. Baca dengan suara keras.
steps.body: Hitung saudara laki-laki dan perempuan bersama sebagai **siblings**: *three siblings: two brothers and one sister*, bukan 'three brothers: two boys and one girl'.

examples.en: My parents live in Medan.
examples.id: Orang tua saya tinggal di Medan.

examples.en: I have three siblings: two brothers and one sister.
examples.id: Saya punya tiga saudara kandung: dua laki-laki dan satu perempuan.

examples.en: My younger brother is a student.
examples.id: Adik laki-laki saya seorang pelajar.

examples.en: Pak Joko and his wife have two daughters.
examples.id: Pak Joko dan istrinya punya dua anak perempuan.

examples.en: My cousin Reza works in Bali.
examples.id: Sepupu saya, Reza, bekerja di Bali.

steps.title: Dengarkan
steps.text: Rina bercerita tentang rumahnya. Tekan play dan dengarkan.

question.prompt: Dengarkan Rina. Dia tinggal dengan siapa?
question.listen: I live in Surabaya with my parents and my grandmother.
question.explanation: Rina bilang **my parents and my grandmother**: ibunya, ayahnya dan neneknya.

steps.title: Ruangan dan perabot
steps.text: Sekarang kita keliling rumah.
steps.body: Ruangan: **living room** (ruang tamu / ruang keluarga), **bedroom**, **kitchen**, **bathroom**. Kamar saja bisa berarti ruangan apa pun, jadi perjelas: kamar tidur = **bedroom**, kamar mandi = **bathroom**. Cukup bilang **the kitchen**, bukan 'the kitchen room'. Perabot: **bed**, **sofa**, **wardrobe** (untuk pakaian), **table**, **chair**, **fridge**.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Ruangan yang mana?

question.prompt: Malam hari, keluarga Budi duduk di sofa dan menonton TV. Mereka ada di ruangan apa?
question.explanation: Sofa dan TV biasanya ada di **living room** (ruang keluarga). Tidak ada 'kitchen room' dalam bahasa Inggris — cukup **the kitchen**.

steps.title: Mendeskripsikan rumah
steps.text: Untuk mendeskripsikan rumah, sebutkan di mana, dengan siapa, dan isinya. Lihat contoh ini.
steps.body: **Di mana:** I live in a house / a flat in ... **Dengan siapa:** I live with ... **Isinya:** My house **has** ... (my house = it, jadi **has**). Taruh kata sifat sebelum kata benda: a **big** bedroom.

examples.en: I live in a small flat in Jakarta.
examples.id: Saya tinggal di apartemen kecil di Jakarta.

examples.en: I live with my wife and my son.
examples.id: Saya tinggal dengan istri dan anak laki-laki saya.

examples.en: Our house has four bedrooms and a garden.
examples.id: Rumah kami punya empat kamar tidur dan sebuah kebun.

examples.en: My bedroom has a bed, a desk and a wardrobe.
examples.id: Di kamar tidur saya ada tempat tidur, meja dan lemari pakaian.

examples.en: The living room is big and bright.
examples.id: Ruang keluarganya besar dan terang.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Pak Joko bercerita tentang apartemennya. Kalimat mana yang benar?

question.explanation: My flat = it, jadi pakai **has** (punya): **My flat has two bedrooms.** 'Have' untuk I, you, we, they, dan 'is two bedrooms' artinya apartemennya ADALAH dua kamar tidur.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang deskripsikan sebuah dapur.

question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Dapur kami kecil tapi bersih.
question.solution: Our kitchen is small but clean.
question.explanation: Mulai dengan ruangannya (**Our kitchen**), lalu **is** + kata sifat. **But** (tapi) menggabungkan dua ide yang berbeda: kecil, tapi bersih.

steps.title: Ringkasan
steps.text: Ini semua kosakatanya dalam satu halaman. Simpan untuk nanti.
